designs.title: R1 · Local pressure-film cells
designs.status_detail: Tooling, wiring and code are supplied. No physical R1 performance has been established.
designs.summary: Add six thin resistive contact cells to the existing finger: two on the hard nail and four on the compliant TPU.
designs.signal: Local electrical conductance; local force estimates require calibration.
designs.best_for: A first contact-coverage and material experiment with common materials.
designs.tradeoff: Handmade laminates, drift, hysteresis, wear and bending behavior need measurement.
sensors: CH0 / CH1
Two N0 pressure-film laminates: 0.10 mm conductive film between copper electrodes and insulating backing
One on the object-facing surface of each hard nail prong
CH2–CH5
Four separate pressure-film cells on conformal silicone saddles
Along the four TPU contact regions, ordered from tip to base
Readout
Pico + two ADS1115 boards; six resistor dividers and reference checks
At the wrist/base; sensing-cell leads run along the finger
designs.placement: Use the R1 CH0–CH5 cut patterns. The two nail pads use the thin N0 construction first; it adds about 0.40 mm nominal mounted thickness. Keep the central nail notch open.

visual.alt: R1's two nail cells CH0/CH1 and four conformal TPU cells CH2–CH5
visual.caption: Sensing locations from the released R1 geometry. Use the cut sheet for the actual fabrication patterns.

resources: Actual-size electrode and carrier cut sheet
Complete runnable source; R1 code is in engineering/firmware/r1 and engineering/software
missing: Assembled specimen evidence and calibrated force/contact results
Repeatability, wear and robot-task qualification
A production FPC replacing the handmade laminates
next_steps: Build the two N0 nail pads first and verify open/short faults.
Add the four TPU cells and test passive bending.
Run the stated force and contact tests across independent specimens.

designs.title: L1 · Whole-finger root force
designs.status_detail: Purchased-cell fixtures, aluminum-carrier CAD and readout code are supplied. Physical fit and force/moment behavior remain untested.
designs.summary: Place a purchased load cell in the complete finger load path while retaining the original contact surfaces.
designs.signal: Aggregate normal force after calibration; it does not provide a contact-location map.
designs.best_for: A separate force benchmark covering normal loads on both nail and TPU.
designs.tradeoff: Adds 20 mm reach and 18.46 mm root width in the CAD. Housing fit, moments, gravity and cable forces remain important.
sensors: Force cell
One TAL220B 5 kg load cell; selected reference SparkFun SEN-14729
Between the fixed jaw carrier and floating finger carrier
Readout
NAU7802, INA219 supply/current monitoring, level shifter and Pico
At the fixed side or wrist
designs.placement: The original finger attaches to the floating carrier. The cell's two solid ends connect separately to the fixed and floating sides. No cable, screw or housing contact may create a parallel load path.

visual.alt: L1 original finger with fixed and floating carriers and a purchased load-cell reference
visual.caption: Actual CAD assembly. The purple cell is a purchased-part reference; fabrication and measurements are pending.

resources: Complete runnable source; L1 code is in engineering/firmware/l1 and engineering/software
missing: Actual drive-housing fit check
Cell and finger force/moment validation
A qualified moving-robot compensation/control system
next_steps: Test the cell in its independent fixture.
Use printed carrier witnesses to check the installed housing.
Machine the aluminum load-path parts only after the preliminary checks, then validate the assembled finger.

designs.title: B1 · Magnetic bending insert
designs.status_detail: Insert/spine CAD, checked sensor PCB files and raw readout code are supplied. No physical force calibration or 20 N qualification is supplied.
designs.summary: Keep the TPU compliant, put four magnets inside it, and read their motion using five fixed magnetic heads. Add two thin nail pads for precision-task contact coverage.
designs.signal: Magnetic-field/deformation observations plus optional nail conductance; calibrated force is not yet available.
designs.best_for: The current magnetic pilot on the existing thin ENPIRE finger.
designs.tradeoff: Adds 3.65 mm global width before screw heads, or 6.05 mm with reserved heads; wires excluded. Assembly, retention and magnetic interference need testing.
sensors: S0–S3
Four MLX90393SLW-ABA-011 heads, each on the custom 8 × 6.4 mm B1 PCB
On the fixed side spine beside the four TPU regions
S4
One identical MLX90393 head
Toward the base as a field reference; it also sees the embedded magnets
M0–M3
Four S-03-01-N, N48, axially magnetized 3 × 1 mm discs
Inside TPU pockets about 34.1, 51.6, 68.6 and 87.0 mm back from the nail tip
T0 / T1
Two R1 N0 pressure-film laminates, recommended for the complete precision-task pilot
On the object-facing surfaces of the two hard nail prongs
Readout
TCA9548A + Pico; ADS1115 when nail pads are fitted
At the wrist/base
designs.placement: Magnets move with the TPU; electronic heads stay fixed. The PCB component faces point toward the magnets. Use the released poses and spine, not a guessed board angle. Enable nail_cells only after installing the nail circuit.

visual.alt: B1 sensor heads S0–S4, TPU magnets M0–M3 and two pressure-film nail pads T0/T1
visual.caption: Labeled placement map for B1 plus the two recommended N0 nail pads. Full coordinates are downloadable below.

A measured B1 force calibration and contact classifier
Across-unit and motor/steel-interference qualification
next_steps: Build one matched original control and a B1 insert.
Verify all magnetic heads and the two nail pads individually.
Record actual motor/jaw/steel conditions before choosing a batch design.

designs.title: B2 · One magnetic PCB
designs.status_detail: B2.1 supplies a routed four-layer PCB with clean independent KiCad DRC, checked mounting CAD, a firmware package and raw recorder. No physical B2 has been tested.
designs.summary: Put all five magnetic sensors, the multiplexer and nail ADC on one shaped PCB. Register it with two spacers and a removable backer; retain B1's TPU, magnets and two thin nail pads.
designs.signal: Raw magnetic observations and nail conductance, with a distinct B2 recording identity. Force still requires physical calibration.
designs.best_for: Testing whether one registered board improves assembly and consistency compared with the five-board B1 pilot.
designs.tradeoff: The routing band is wider within the original side profile. Whole-board repair cost, magnetic interference and calibration transfer still need measurement.
sensors: Five MLX90393SLW-ABA-011 ICs
On one rigid PCB at the released B1 head positions and orientations
M0–M3
The same four 3 × 1 mm N48 magnets and TPU cartridge for the first comparison
Inside the B1-style TPU pockets
T0 / T1
Retain the two N0 nail pads in the initial comparison
On the nail prongs; their leads are still required
TCA9548ARGER multiplexer + ADS1115IDGSR nail ADC
In the base bay on that same PCB
Pico
Raspberry Pi Pico RP2040 running yam-b2/1
At the wrist/base; J1 connects 3V3, GND, SCL/GP5 and SDA/GP4
designs.placement: The component face points inward toward the magnets. Two shouldered spacers register the board on the original B1 mount axes; a removable backer holds it. J1 has four upstream conductors. J2 has four separate nail leads, with a 100 kΩ continuity resistor at each nail pad. TP1–TP5 are test lands, not head-wire connectors.

visual.alt: B2 single board with S0-S4 sensor positions, M0-M3 magnets and the two nail pads
visual.caption: Placement from the B2.1 design. Sensor poses are preserved; the connecting band and mounting parts are revised. Physical testing remains pending.

next_steps: Print the board witness, backer and locating spacers and check the actual installed drive.
Populate one PCB, connect both nail pads and verify every channel and fault condition.
Record the common bench tests with matched B1 controls before deciding whether B2 is better.

designs.title: C1 · Differential-strain root force
designs.status_detail: An analytical model and metal coupon CAD exist. There is no complete YAM adapter, assembled bridge, firmware or qualified force sensor.
designs.summary: Measure aggregate normal force using two strain bridges on a metal load-path element, leaving the nail and soft contact region passive.
designs.signal: Normal force from the difference of calibrated bending measurements in the ideal model; no local contact map.
designs.best_for: Studying a force path that does not infer load from a magnetic field.
designs.tradeoff: Gauge bonding, gain matching, thermal drift, gravity, cross-axis loads and short-beam end effects need substantial work.
sensors: Station 1 / 2
Two 350 Ω full strain bridges, eight foil gauges total; exact gauge/bonding selection pending
On opposite faces of the active beam, at 5 and 13 mm from the assumed fixed boundary
Readout candidate
Two ADS1232 converters, one per bridge
On fixed electronics near the beam or wrist; no completed C1 readout is supplied
designs.placement: The coupon has an 18 mm active section, 25 mm width and 8 mm thickness, with clamp ends. All intended finger loads must enter beyond both sensing stations and avoid parallel load paths. The coupon itself does not establish gripper mounting or reach.

visual.alt: C1 metal coupon with two strain stations and an analytical stiffness comparison
visual.caption: Gauge rectangles mark locations, not finalized gauge footprints. The short beam still needs 3D FEA and measurements.

resources: Metal coupon STL — not a plastic force part
Analytical model and generator in the complete source
missing: 3D structural and gauge-area analysis
Selected gauge footprint, bonding process and complete electronics
A gripper adapter and controlled installed load path
Force calibration, motion compensation and durability evidence
next_steps: Use L1 as the existing purchased-cell force baseline.
Evaluate the C1 coupon and matched bridges before designing an installed adapter.
Test moment rejection, thermal drift, unloaded poses and no-contact motions.

designs.title: Rigid nail · Sense at its base
designs.status_detail: This is a proposed sensing architecture. No ENPIRE nail mechanism, selected sensor BOM, manufacturing CAD or firmware has been completed.
designs.summary: Keep a bare, thin rigid nail and measure its loading through a controlled support at the nail's base instead of adding a pressure-film laminate to its surface.
designs.signal: Intended nail force and possibly torque; achievable axes and accuracy are not established.
designs.best_for: A future redesign when thin-tip access or surface-pad wear becomes the main problem.
designs.tradeoff: Needs a new support/load path, overload behavior, calibration and a way to preserve tip-position accuracy.
sensors: Base sensing
Not selected: magnetic displacement sensing or bonded strain sensing are options
At the controlled nail support behind the leading gripping surface
Commercial benchmark
XELA uSCu ALHA-N is a reference architecture, not a selected ENPIRE component
Allegro-specific fingertip; dimensions, range and custom integration must be checked
designs.placement: The nail surface contacts the object. Its support transmits load to sensing elements at the base. The sensing mechanism, flexures and readout locations are not finalized. This concept is not included in the B2 board witness.
resources: B1 with the current N0 nail pads
missing: An ENPIRE-specific mechanism and CAD
Sensor selection, placement dimensions and electronics
Normal/shear/torque load-path and overload design
Any prototype measurements or manufacturing files
next_steps: Define needed force axes and allowed nail motion for the actual tasks.
Choose the support/sensing mechanism and produce an independent mechanical design.
Validate a nail module before combining it with the soft-finger sensing system.

designs.title: Recessed magnetic board · Revise the frame
designs.status_detail: Only translation-based field and clearance scenarios exist. No recessed hard-frame CAD or approved sensor travel is supplied.
designs.summary: Explore placing the magnetic board closer to the embedded magnets to increase signal and potentially reduce side bulk.
designs.signal: Magnetic deformation observations, as in B1; a new gain/range choice may be required.
designs.best_for: A later frame redesign if measured B1 signal quality or side thickness is unacceptable.
designs.tradeoff: Less space for TPU motion, failed stock-frame clearance screens, and possible readout-range overflow.
sensors: S0–S4
The B1 MLX90393 heads used as the study basis
Translated inward in the model while retaining their length/height positions
M0–M3
The B1 magnets used as the study basis
Held at their released positions for this comparison
designs.placement: The study compares PCB planes at the original native X≈8.44 mm and hypothetical 6.0, 4.0 and 2.8 mm planes. The inward cases fail the conservative existing-frame screen. They are not installation instructions.

visual.alt: Calculated signal increase and configured range consumption as the board moves inward
visual.caption: Field/clearance scenarios only. No modified frame, load deformation or safe travel was modeled.

resources: Recessed-board scenarios in the magnetic study JSON
Scenario calculator in the complete source
missing: A redesigned frame with verified structural load paths
Motion/clearance checks under load
A selected readout configuration and saturation analysis over actual motion
Manufacturing files for a recessed frame
next_steps: Measure whether the existing B1 actually has a signal or bulk problem.
Design the frame recess and mechanical protection if the change is justified.
Recheck field range, contact sensitivity and clearance before loading the new part.

designs.title: Flexible matrix · Dense resistive contact array
designs.status_detail: No routed ENPIRE flex circuit, complete material stack or firmware is supplied for this approach.
designs.summary: Replace separate hand-built resistive cells with a denser patterned contact array that could be manufactured as a flexible circuit or printed laminate.
designs.signal: Per-pixel electrical response; pressure/force and crosstalk behavior require calibration.
designs.best_for: Denser local contact coverage when custom flex manufacture is justified.
designs.tradeoff: Crosstalk, contact-area dependence, fatigue, sealing and custom fork-shaped artwork remain design work.
sensors: Array
Not selected; FlexiTac/HiPi-style resistive matrices are references
Across the nail and compliant contact regions using application-specific artwork
Readout
Not finalized for this finger
On the fixed electronics, connected through a flex tail
designs.placement: A generic rectangular array does not define the narrow fork geometry. The nail notch and flexing TPU require separate layout and fatigue decisions.
missing: Exact sensor and manufacturing stack
ENPIRE-shaped routed FPC and readout
Bending, crosstalk, sealing and force results
next_steps: Choose the array architecture and fabrication process.
Prototype one small coupon and compare crosstalk and bending artifacts with R1.
Design the fork-shaped production artwork only after the material/readout tests.

designs.title: Capacitive skin · Shielded contact cells
designs.status_detail: A sensing approach and converter reference are identified. No ENPIRE capacitor stack, routed flex or calibrated sensor is supplied.
designs.summary: Use shaped capacitive compression cells to obtain thin local contact sensing without permanent magnets.
designs.signal: Capacitance changes; force depends on the mechanical dielectric structure and calibration.
designs.best_for: A possible alternative when magnetic interference is unacceptable.
designs.tradeoff: Dielectric creep, parasitics, moisture, shielding and interconnect strain need control.
sensors: Contact cells
Not finalized: electrode/dielectric cells on local rigid islands
Under the intended contact patches; dimensions and stack are not selected
Readout reference
TI FDC1004
On fixed electronics close to the sensing connections, with an appropriate shield layout
designs.placement: The sensor is the mechanical capacitor, not the converter IC alone. A flexing finger needs a layout that separates contact compression from unwanted bending/strain response.
missing: A selected dielectric and electrode stack
Mechanical islands, flex routing, shielding and sealing
ENPIRE CAD, PCB files, firmware and force data
next_steps: Make and characterize a single compression coupon.
Measure contact response separately from bending, moisture and nearby-object effects.
Develop a shaped array if the coupon supports the required range and durability.

designs.title: Pneumatic finger · Internal air channels
designs.status_detail: FORTE is a relevant published reference. No ENPIRE adaptation or 20 N version has been designed here.
designs.summary: Sense deformation of a compliant finger through changes in internal air pressure, with pressure transducers located away from the contact surface.
designs.signal: Pressure measurements interpreted as force/slip through a validated mechanical model.
designs.best_for: A passive soft interface with electronics at the wrist.
designs.tradeoff: Sealing, tubing, temperature/volume effects and the demonstrated force range require attention.
sensors: Soft interface
FORTE-style internal air channels are the reference
Within a redesigned compliant finger
Reference transducers
FORTE's hardware guide lists ELVR-L01D-F1RD-C-NA3F transducers
At the wrist/base, connected by tubes; this is not a selected ENPIRE BOM
designs.placement: The compliant chamber is the contact element. Tubes connect it to fixed pressure sensors. The published reference reports a 0–8 N experiment; a 20 N ENPIRE design still needs new range and mechanical work.
missing: ENPIRE-specific chambers and tubing route
Verified sealing, range and overload behavior
A 20 N calibration and hard-nail contact strategy
next_steps: Reproduce a reference pressure chamber before modifying the finger.
Measure leaks, drift and response over the intended force range.
Design a separate hard-nail sensing path if nail-only contacts must be covered.

designs.title: Optical finger · Observe contact deformation
designs.status_detail: Optical compliant fingers were reviewed. No optical ENPIRE finger, camera layout or sensor software is supplied.
designs.summary: Use illumination and a camera to observe a deformable sensing surface and recover richer contact geometry.
designs.signal: Images of contact/deformation; geometry, force and slip estimates require calibration and processing.
designs.best_for: Tasks that need dense contact shape or texture information.
designs.tradeoff: Optical path, lighting, gel fabrication, processing and the thin-nail interface require a substantial redesign.
sensors: Sensing surface
Not selected; Baby Fin Ray is a compliant optical reference
At the object-contact interface
Camera and lighting
Not selected for ENPIRE
Inside or toward the base of a redesigned finger, with a clear view of the sensing surface
designs.placement: The camera observes the back of a deforming surface through an engineered optical path. A camera body attached to the current finger does not make the opaque TPU/nail tactile.
missing: Camera/lens/illumination selection and optical layout
Gel, reflector and protective surface process
A nail-coverage solution and ENPIRE fabrication files
Calibration and task data
next_steps: Define whether dense contact imagery is actually required.
Prototype the optical path and surface visibility during bending.
Validate a redesigned finger rather than treating the system as an add-on film.

designs.title: MEMS force button · Controlled point loading
designs.status_detail: A commercial force-sensor family was reviewed. No controlled-load mechanism or ENPIRE integration has been designed.
designs.summary: Route a known compressive load through a packaged digital force sensor instead of inferring force from a magnetic skin.
designs.signal: Force applied to the sensor's mechanical contact element; gripper force requires a controlled load path.
designs.best_for: An integration study when a compact packaged force element is useful.
designs.tradeoff: Range alone does not establish low-force accuracy. Preload, side loading, moments and temperature remain important.
sensors: Reference device
Honeywell FMA family, 25 N option; not a selected production part
Under a designed load button/plunger on fixed electronics
Mechanical coupling
Not designed
Between the finger's force path and the sensor contact element
designs.placement: The intended force must reach the sensor through its specified contact interface. It is not a flexible pressure sheet to glue across the TPU or nail.
resources: Accuracy/range conditions in the architecture study
missing: A selected ordering code and mechanically valid coupling
Gripper mounting, side-load/moment protection and overload design
Low-force and 20 N installed measurements
next_steps: Check the exact part's specified conditions against the task.
Build and test its mechanical coupling with an independent force reference.
Compare installed force behavior with L1 before choosing this route.
